Bounds on the minimum distance of locally recoverable codes

Sascha Kurz Affiliation: Mathematisches Institut, Universität Bayreuth, D-95440 Bayreuth, Germany, sascha.kurz@uni-bayreuth.de
 and  
Department of Data Science, Friedrich-Alexander-Universitäät Erlangen-Nürnberg, D-91058 Erlangen, Germany, sascha.kurz@fau.de
Abstract

We consider locally recoverable codes (LRCs) and aim to determine the smallest possible length n=nq​(k,d,r)n=n_{q}(k,d,r) of a linear [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-code with locality rr. For k≤7k\leq 7 we exactly determine all values of n2​(k,d,2)n_{2}(k,d,2) and for k≤6k\leq 6 we exactly determine all values of n2​(k,d,1)n_{2}(k,d,1). For the ternary field we also state a few numerical results. As a general result we prove that nq​(k,d,r)n_{q}(k,d,r) equals the Griesmer bound if the minimum Hamming distance dd is sufficiently large and all other parameters are fixed.

Mathematics Subject Classification: 94B27, 94B05
Keywords: linear codes, locally recoverable codes, data storage, bounds for parameters

1 Introduction

A code over a finite alphabet is called locally recoverable (LRC) if every symbol in the encoding is a function of a small number of (at most rr) other symbols. They have e.g. applications in distributed storage and communications. Here we will consider linear codes over a finite field 𝔽q\mathbb{F}_{q} as alphabet. An [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-code CC is a kk-dimensional subspace of 𝔽qn\mathbb{F}_{q}^{n} with minimum Hamming distance (at least) dd. We also speak of [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-codes if we do not want to specify the minimum Hamming distance. A code symbol is said to have rr-locality if it can be repaired from at most rr other code symbols. An (n,k,r)q(n,k,r)_{q}-LRC is an [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-code with rr-locality for all code symbols. For given parameters nn, kk and alphabet size qq one would like to have codes with small locality rr, allowing e.g. a fast recovery process when the code is used for distributed storage, and a large minimum Hamming distance dd, in order to deal with possible errors in the transmission. However, there is a natural tradeoff between minimizing rr and maximizing dd. To this end we mention the bound

d≤n−k−⌈kr⌉+2d\leq n-k-\left\lceil\frac{k}{r}\right\rceil+2 (1)

by Gopalan et al. [GHSY12], which reduces to the classical Singleton bound when r=kr=k. Surely we have 1≤r≤k1\leq r\leq k and MDS codes attain the bound for r=kr=k. Replicating each symbol in an MDS code twice yields codes attaining the bound for r=1r=1. If the field size is sufficiently large then the upper bound (1) can always be attained with equality [GHSY12]. Further constructions requiring smaller field sizes can e.g. be found in [TB14], i.e. q≥n+1q\geq n+1 assuming that r+1r+1 divides nn, see also [LXY18, TBGC15]. However, small finite fields as alphabets are often desirable for practical reasons [GC14]. In [TPD16] the search for constructions meeting the stated bound (1) with equality was stated as an open problem. Constructions for the binary case can e.g. be found in [GC14, HYUS15, HYUS16]. For q∈{2,3,4}q\in\{2,3,4\} all cases where Inequality (1) can be attained with equality were characterized in [HXC16], [HXC17], and [XKG22], respectively. For q≥n+1q\geq n+1 codes with d=n−k−⌈kr⌉+1d=n-k-\left\lceil\tfrac{k}{r}\right\rceil+1, i.e. one less than the upper bound (1), indeed exist [TB14]. Using the function koptq​(n,d)k_{\operatorname{opt}}^{q}(n,d) for the maximum possible dimension kk of an [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-code the bound

k≤mint∈ℕ⁡{r​t+koptq​(n−t⁡(r+1),d)}k\leq\min_{t\in\mathbb{N}}\left\{rt+k_{\operatorname{opt}}^{q}(n-t(r+1),d)\right\} (2)

for [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-codes with locality rr was obtained in [CM15] and e.g. used in [HXS+20] to conclude explicit parametric bounds on codes with a given locality.

Another classical bound for linear codes is the Griesmer bound [Gri60] relating the minimal possible length nq​(k,d)n_{q}(k,d) of an [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-code to its other parameters:

nq​(k,d)≥gq​(k,d):=∑i=0k−1⌈dqi⌉.n_{q}(k,d)\geq g_{q}(k,d):=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left\lceil\frac{d}{q^{i}}\right\rceil\!\!. (3)

Solomon and Stifler gave a construction showing that this bound can be attained for any given parameters kk and qq if dd is sufficiently large [SS65]. Consequently, the determination of the function nq​(k,⋅)n_{q}(k,\cdot) becomes a finite problem for each pair of parameters kk, qq. For k≤7k\leq 7, the function n2​(k,⋅)n_{2}(k,\cdot) has been completely determined in [BM73] and [vT81]. After a lot of work of different authors, the determination of n2​(8,d)n_{2}(8,d) has been completed in [BJV00]. Here we will show that for any given pair of parameters kk, qq there exist (n,k,2)q(n,k,2)_{q}-LRCs and (n,k,1)q(n,k,1)_{q}-LRCs with length n=nq​(k,d)n=n_{q}(k,d) and minimum Hamming distance dd assuming that dd is sufficiently large. So, also the determination of the largest possible Hamming distance of (n,k,2)q(n,k,2)_{q}- and (n,k,1)q(n,k,1)_{q}-LRCs becomes a finite problem for any parameters kk and qq.

In the literature also special subclasses of LRCs, like e.g. maximally recoverable codes [CHL07], have been considered. The required field size of a maximally recoverable codes was e.g. improved in [GWFHH19]. There the authors used matroid theory, see also [GFHWH17, WFHEH16], to show non-existence of some codes with prescribed parameters by characterising linearity over small fields via forbidden uniform minors. In [PKLK12] the authors introduced the notion of (r,δ)(r,\delta)-LRCs. Corresponding LP and other bounds can e.g. be found in [GJR23]. In [GFHWH19] the authors introduced a slight variant of the definition of locality, called dimension-locality, and study corresponding bounds.

The remaining part of this paper is structured as follows. In Section 2 we introduce the necessary preliminaries. A geometric reformulation of locality is then discussed in Section 3 and used to bound the minimal possible lengths of [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-codes with locality rr. Then we summarize several constructions and non-existence results for LRCs in Section 4. For several small parameter sets we were able to completely determine the minimum possible length of an [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-code with locality r∈{1,2}r\in\{1,2\} as a function of the minimum Hamming distance dd. We close the paper in Section 5 by stating enumeration results for [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-codes with locality rr for some small parameters. The focus on exact values for small parameters is thought as a supplement to the existing literature which mainly considers different general bounds. While we cannot draw asymptotic conclusions from our obtained data, we remark that the number of used nodes nn is typically rather small in many real-world applications, see e.g. HDFS-Xorbas used by Facebook [APD+13] and Windows Azure storage [HSX+12]. Since variants and extensions of LRCs are comprehensive, we refrain from discussing similar results for some of them.

2 Preliminaries

For a given linear code CC we denote its minimum Hamming distance by d⁡(C)d(C) and the dual code by C⟂C^{\perp}. Apart from the field size qq, the length nn, the dimension kk, and the minimum Hamming distance dd of a linear [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-code we consider the locality as an additional parameter.

Definition 1.

A (linear) code C⊆𝔽qnC\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{q}^{n} has locality rr if for every coordinate i∈{1,…,n}i\in\{1,\dots,n\} there exists a set Si⊆{1,…,n}S_{i}\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\} with i∉Sii\notin S_{i}, |Si|≤r\left|S_{i}\right|\leq r, and if cj=cj′c_{j}=c^{\prime}_{j} for all j∈Sij\in S_{i} for two codewords c,c′∈Cc,c^{\prime}\in C then we have xi=yix_{i}=y_{i}.

We also speak of a locally recoverable code (LRC). The set SiS_{i} is called a recovery set for coordinate ii. Denoting the projection map onto the coordinates from some set S⊆{1,…,n}S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\} by πS\pi_{S}, we can introduce recovery functions fi:πSi​(C)→𝔽qf_{i}\colon\pi_{S_{i}}(C)\to\mathbb{F}_{q} satisfying fi​(πSi​(c))=cif_{i}(\pi_{S_{i}}(c))=c_{i} for all c∈Cc\in C and all 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n.

Lemma 2.

([ABH+18, Lemma 10]) Let CC be an [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-code and SiS_{i} a recovery set for coordinate 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n with recovery function fif_{i}. Then, fif_{i} is an 𝔽q\mathbb{F}_{q}-linear map.

So, we can express the locality of a given linear code CC via the existence of certain codewords in its dual code C⟂C^{\perp}:

Lemma 3.

A linear [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-code CC has locality r≥1r\geq 1 iff for every coordinate 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n there exists a dual codeword c∈C⟂c\in C^{\perp} with weight at most r+1r+1 that contains ii in its support.

Definition 4.

An [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-code CC is non-degenerate, if there does not exist a coordinate 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n such that ci=0c_{i}=0 for all codewords c∈Cc\in C. We call CC projective if the coordinates of the codewords are linearly independent; that is, there exists no coordinate i≠j∈{1,…,n}i\neq j\in\{1,\dots,n\} and λ∈𝔽q\{0}\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_{q}\backslash\{0\} such that ci=λ⋅cjc_{i}=\lambda\cdot c_{j} for every c∈Cc\in C.

In other words, a linear code CC is non-degenerate if every column of a generator matrix GG of CC is non-zero. If no column of a generator matrix CC is a scalar multiple of another column, then the corresponding linear code CC is projective.

By PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) we denote the finite projective geometry of dimension k−1k-1 and order qq. A well-known and often exploited interpretation of non-degenerated linear codes is the following. The columns of a generator matrix GG of a non-degenerated [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-code CC may be interpreted as points of the projective space PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q). In the other direction, a multiset of points ℳ\mathcal{M} in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) is a mapping from the set of points to the natural integers. Here, for each point PP we call ℳ⁡(P)\mathcal{M}(P) the multiplicity of PP. The cardinality |ℳ||\mathcal{M}| of our multiset ℳ\mathcal{M} is the sum over all point multiplicities and equals the length nn of the corresponding (non-degenerate) code CC. By γ⁡(ℳ)\gamma(\mathcal{M}) we denote the maximum point multiplicity of ℳ\mathcal{M}. So, we have d⁡(C⟂)=2d(C^{\perp})=2 iff γ⁡(ℳ)≥2\gamma(\mathcal{M})\geq 2 and γ⁡(ℳ)=1\gamma(\mathcal{M})=1 iff CC is projective. Using the geometric language we call 2−2-, 3−3-, 4−4-, and (k−1)(k-1)-dimensional subspaces lines, planes, solids, and hyperplanes, respectively. So, each dual codeword c∈C⟂c\in C^{\perp} of weight three geometrically corresponds to a triple of points spanning a line and each dual codeword of weight 22 geometrically corresponds to a point with multiplicity at least 22. We call a multiset of points ℳ\mathcal{M} in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) spanning if the points with positive multiplicity span the ambient space PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q). The multiset of points corresponding to an [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-code is always spanning. In the other direction we have that a multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) might correspond to an [n,k′]q[n,k^{\prime}]_{q}-code with k′<kk^{\prime}<k. The minimum Hamming distance of CC is at least dd iff we have ℳ⁡(H)≤n−d\mathcal{M}(H)\leq n-d for every hyperplane HH, where ℳ⁡(H)\mathcal{M}(H) is defined as the sum of all multiplicities of the points contained in HH, i.e., ℳ⁡(H)=∑P≤Hℳ⁡(P)\mathcal{M}(H)=\sum_{P\leq H}\mathcal{M}(P). Writing [nk]q\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{k}_{q} for the number of kk-dimensional subspaces in PG⁡(n−1,q)\PG(n-1,q) we can state that each tt-dimensional subspace contains [t1]q\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{t}{1}_{q} points and PG⁡(n−1,q)\PG(n-1,q) contains [nn−1]q=[n1]q\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{n-1}_{q}=\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{1}_{q} hyperplanes in total. Since each point is contained in [k−11]q\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k-1}{1}_{q} hyperplanes and each pair of different points is contained in [k−21]q\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k-2}{1}_{q} hyperplanes, assuming k≥3k\geq 3, we have

(n−d)⋅[k−11]q≥∑H:P≤Hℳ(H)=n⋅[k−21]q+qk−2⋅ℳ(P)(n-d)\cdot\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k-1}{1}_{q}\geq\sum_{H\,:\,P\leq H}\mathcal{M}(H)=n\cdot\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k-2}{1}_{q}+q^{k-2}\cdot\mathcal{M}(P) (4)

for every point PP. Similarly,

(n−d)⋅qk−1≥∑H:P≰Hℳ(H)=qk−2⋅(n−ℳ(P))(n-d)\cdot q^{k-1}\geq\sum_{H\,:\,P\not\leq H}\mathcal{M}(H)=q^{k-2}\cdot(n-\mathcal{M}(P)) (5)

for every point PP. For two multisets of points ℳ,ℳ′∈PG⁡(k−1,q)\mathcal{M},\mathcal{M}^{\prime}\in\PG(k-1,q) we write ℳ+ℳ′\mathcal{M}+\mathcal{M}^{\prime} for the multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) with multiplicity ℳ​(P)+ℳ′​(P)\mathcal{M}(P)+\mathcal{M}^{\prime}(P) for every point PP. Similarly, for each multiset ℳ\mathcal{M} in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) and each integer t≥1t\geq 1 we write t⋅ℳt\cdot\mathcal{M} for the multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) with multiplicity t⋅ℳ⁡(P)t\cdot\mathcal{M}(P) for every point PP.

3 Geometric reformulation of locality and minimal possible lengths of [𝐧,𝐤,𝐝]𝐪\mathbf{[n,k,d]_{q}}-codes with locality 𝐫\mathbf{r}

Directly from Lemma 3 we conclude:

Lemma 5.

Let CC be a linear [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-code and ℳ\mathcal{M} be the corresponding multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) of cardinality nn. Then, CC has locality r≥1r\geq 1 iff for every point PP with positive multiplicity ℳ⁡(P)≥1\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 1 either ℳ⁡(P)≥2\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 2 or there are t≤rt\leq r points with positive multiplicity and being different from PP that span an tt-dimensional subspace SS with P≤SP\leq S.

So, locality is also a geometric property of a multiset of points ℳ\mathcal{M} and we directly say that ℳ\mathcal{M} has locality rr is its corresponding code has locality rr. We remark that especially the locality of a linear code does not depend on a specific representation in terms of a generator matrix with is e.g. different for private information retrieval (PIR) codes, see [KY21, Proposition 9]. For small values of rr we can also spell out the condition of Lemma 5 more directly.

Lemma 6.

Let CC be a linear [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-code and ℳ\mathcal{M} be the corresponding multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) of cardinality nn. Then, CC has locality 11 iff every point PP with positive multiplicity ℳ⁡(P)≥1\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 1 has multiplicity at least 22.

Or in other words, a non-empty multiset of points has locality 11 iff no point has multiplicity exactly 11.

Lemma 7.

Let CC be a linear [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-code and ℳ\mathcal{M} be the corresponding multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) of cardinality nn. Then, CC has locality 22 iff for every point PP with positive multiplicity ℳ⁡(P)≥1\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 1 we have ℳ⁡(P)≥2\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 2 or there exist points Q,RQ,R with |{P,Q,R}|=3|\{P,Q,R\}|=3, dim(⟨P,Q,R⟩)=2\dim(\langle P,Q,R\rangle)=2, and ℳ⁡(Q),ℳ⁡(R)≥1\mathcal{M}(Q),\mathcal{M}(R)\geq 1.

A multiset of points ℳ\mathcal{M} over the binary field 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2} has locality 22 iff every point with multiplicity 11 is contained in a full line, i.e., all three points of the line have positive multiplicity.

Lemma 8.

Let CC be an [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-code with dual minimum distance d⟂=3d^{\perp}=3. If the number of dual codewords of weight 33 is less than (q−1)⋅n/3(q-1)\cdot n/3, then the locality of CC is larger than 22.

Proof.

Due to Lemma 3 the locality of CC is at least 22. So, due to Lemma 7, any point with positive multiplicity w.r.t. the corresponding multiset of points ℳ\mathcal{M} has to be contained in a line that contains at least three points with positive multiplicity. Our nn points with positive multiplicity cannot be covered by fewer than n/3n/3 such lines. However, since each such line corresponds to (q−1)(q-1) dual codewords of weight 33, we obtain a contradiction. ∎

Similar to the notion of nq​(k,d)n_{q}(k,d) let nq​(k,d,r)n_{q}(k,d,r) denote the minimal possible length of an [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-code with locality rr, i.e., the minimum possible cardinality of a spanning multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) with locality rr. So, clearly we have

nq(k,d,r)≥nq(k,d)≥gq(k,d)=∑i=0k−1⌈dqi.⌉n_{q}(k,d,r)\geq n_{q}(k,d)\geq g_{q}(k,d)=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left\lceil\frac{d}{q^{i}}.\right\rceil (6)

and nq​(k,d,r)≤nq​(k,d,r′)n_{q}(k,d,r)\leq n_{q}(k,d,r^{\prime}) for all r≥r′r\geq r^{\prime}. In Theorem 10 we will show nq​(k,d,r)=gq​(k,d)n_{q}(k,d,r)=g_{q}(k,d) for sufficiently large dd and fixed parameters qq, kk, and rr.

Example 9.

Let ℳ\mathcal{M} be the (multi-)set of points in 𝒫⁡(k−1,q)\mathcal{P}(k-1,q) where each point has multiplicity exactly 11. Then, ℳ\mathcal{M} has cardinality qk−1q−1=[k1]q\tfrac{q^{k}-1}{q-1}=\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k}{1}_{q} and each hyperplane HH has multiplicity ℳ⁡(H)=qk−1−1q−1=[k−11]q\mathcal{M}(H)=\tfrac{q^{k-1}-1}{q-1}=\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k-1}{1}_{q}, so that |ℳ|−ℳ⁡(H)=qk−1|\mathcal{M}|-\mathcal{M}(H)=q^{k-1}. The corresponding linear code is called kk-dimensional qq-ary simplex code and has parameters [n,k,d]q=[[k1]q,k,qk−1]q[n,k,d]_{q}=\left[\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k}{1}_{q},k,q^{k-1}\right]_{q}. If k≥2k\geq 2 then ℳ\mathcal{M} has locality r=2r=2 since each point has multiplicity 11 and each point is contained in at least one line (whose points also have multiplicity 11 each). For each integer t≥1t\geq 1 the multiset of points t⋅ℳt\cdot\mathcal{M} has cardinality t⋅[k1]qt\cdot\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k}{1}_{q} and locality 11 iff t≥2t\geq 2. The corresponding linear code, called tt-fold simplex code, has parameters [n,k,d]q=[t⋅[k1]q,k,t⋅qk−1]q[n,k,d]_{q}=\left[t\cdot\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k}{1}_{q},k,t\cdot q^{k-1}\right]_{q}. Note that we have n=gq​(k,d)n=g_{q}(k,d) for all t≥1t\geq 1.

Theorem 10.

Let qq be an arbitrary prime power, k∈ℕ≥2k\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}, and r∈ℕ≥1r\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}. If dd is sufficiently large, then we have nq​(k,d,r)=gq​(k,d)n_{q}(k,d,r)=g_{q}(k,d).

Proof.

It suffices to prove the statement for locality r=1r=1. Due to [SS65] there exists a constant d′d^{\prime} (depending on kk and qq) such that for all d≥d′d\geq d^{\prime} we have nq​(k,d)=gk​(k,d)n_{q}(k,d)=g_{k}(k,d).11 1 For k≥3k\geq 3, e.g. d≥(k−2)​qk−1−(k−1)​qk−2+1d\geq(k-2)q^{k-1}-(k-1)q^{k-2}+1 is sufficient [Mar97]. For d≥d′d\geq d^{\prime} consider an [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-code with n=gq​(k,d)n=g_{q}(k,d) and let ℳ\mathcal{M} be the corresponding multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q). Setting t:=⌊d/qk−1⌋t:=\left\lfloor d/q^{k-1}\right\rfloor, we have d≥t⋅qk−1d\geq t\cdot q^{k-1} and n≤(t+1)⋅[k1]qn\leq(t+1)\cdot\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k}{1}_{q}. Using this and Inequality (5) we conclude

ℳ⁡(P)≥n⁡(1−q)+d​q≥t−qk\mathcal{M}(P)\geq n(1-q)+dq\geq t-q^{k}

for every point PP. So, if dd is sufficiently large, then we have t≥qk+2t\geq q^{k}+2 and ℳ\mathcal{M} has locality 11 due to Lemma 6. ∎

So for every set of parameters qq, kk, and rr the determination of nq​(k,d,r)n_{q}(k,d,r), as a function of dd, is a finite problem. In principle we can determine the exact value of nq​(k,d,r)n_{q}(k,d,r) for each given set of parameters as the optimum target value of an integer linear program (ILP). We will spell out the details for r∈{1,2}r\in\{1,2\} and leave the general problem as an exercise for the interested reader.

Proposition 11.

Let qq, kk, and dd be arbitrary but fixed parameters. Then, nq​(k,d,1)n_{q}(k,d,1) is given as the optimum target value of the following ILP:

min⁡n\displaystyle\min n subject to
∑P∈𝒫xP\displaystyle\sum_{P\in\mathcal{P}}x_{P} =\displaystyle= n\displaystyle n
x⟨ei⟩\displaystyle x_{\langle e_{i}\rangle} ≥\displaystyle\geq 1∀1≤i≤k\displaystyle 1\quad\forall 1\leq i\leq k
∑P∈𝒫:P≤HxP\displaystyle\sum_{P\in\mathcal{P}\,:\ P\leq H}x_{P} ≤\displaystyle\leq n−d∀H∈ℋ\displaystyle n-d\quad\forall H\in\mathcal{H}
xP\displaystyle x_{P} ≥\displaystyle\geq 2​yP∀P∈𝒫\displaystyle 2y_{P}\quad\forall P\in\mathcal{P}
xP\displaystyle x_{P} ≤\displaystyle\leq Λ​yP∀P∈𝒫\displaystyle\Lambda y_{P}\quad\forall P\in\mathcal{P}
xP\displaystyle x_{P} ∈\displaystyle\in ℕ∀P∈𝒫\displaystyle\mathbb{N}\quad\forall P\in\mathcal{P}
yP\displaystyle y_{P} ∈\displaystyle\in {0,1}∀P∈𝒫,\displaystyle\{0,1\}\quad\forall P\in\mathcal{P},

where eie_{i} denotes the iith unit vector, 𝒫\mathcal{P} denotes the set of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q), ℋ\mathcal{H} denotes the set of hyperplanes in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q), and Λ\Lambda is a sufficiently large constant.

Proof.

For a feasible solution of the stated ILP we can define a multiset of points ℳ\mathcal{M} via ℳ⁡(P)=xP∈ℕ\mathcal{M}(P)=x_{P}\in\mathbb{N} for all points P∈𝒫P\in\mathcal{P}. The cardinality of ℳ\mathcal{M} is given by ∑P∈𝒫ℳ⁡(P)=∑P∈𝒫xP=n\sum_{P\in\mathcal{P}}\mathcal{M}(P)=\sum_{P\in\mathcal{P}}x_{P}=n. Since ℳ(H)=∑P∈𝒫:P≤HxP≤n−d\mathcal{M}(H)=\sum_{P\in\mathcal{P}\,:\ P\leq H}x_{P}\leq n-d the corresponding linear code CC has Hamming distance at least dd. Since ℳ⁡(⟨ei⟩)=x⟨ei⟩≥1\mathcal{M}(\langle e_{i}\rangle)=x_{\langle e_{i}\rangle}\geq 1 the multiset ℳ\mathcal{M} is spanning, i.e., the linear code CC has dimension kk. For any point P∈𝒫P\in\mathcal{P} the constraints xP≥2​yPx_{P}\geq 2y_{P} and xP≤Λ​yPx_{P}\leq\Lambda y_{P} are equivalent to xP=0x_{P}=0 for yP=0y_{P}=0 and to 2≤xP≤Λ2\leq x_{P}\leq\Lambda for yP=1y_{P}=1, i.e., we have ℳ⁡(P)≠1\mathcal{M}(P)\neq 1. Thus, ℳ\mathcal{M} and CC have locality 11.

For the other direction consider an [n,k,q]q[n,k,q]_{q}-code C′C^{\prime} and its corresponding multiset of points ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime}. Since ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime} is spanning there exists an isomorphic multisets of points ℳ\mathcal{M} with ℳ⁡(⟨ei⟩)≥1\mathcal{M}(\langle e_{i}\rangle)\geq 1 for all 1≤i≤k1\leq i\leq k. Let CC denote the [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-code corresponding to ℳ\mathcal{M}. Setting xP=ℳ⁡(P)∈ℕx_{P}=\mathcal{M}(P)\in\mathbb{N} for all points P∈𝒫P\in\mathcal{P} all constraints that do not involve a yy-variable are satisfied. If C′C^{\prime} has locality 11, so does CC and ℳ\mathcal{M}. From Lemma 6 we conclude xP=ℳ⁡(P)≠1x_{P}=\mathcal{M}(P)\neq 1 for all P∈𝒫P\in\mathcal{P}. So, if ℳ⁡(P)=0\mathcal{M}(P)=0 we can set yP=1y_{P}=1. If 2≤ℳ⁡(P)≤Λ2\leq\mathcal{M}(P)\leq\Lambda for a sufficiently large constant Λ\Lambda we can set yP=1y_{P}=1. With this all constraints are satisfied, i.e., we have constructed a feasible solution of the above ILP. We remark that choosing Λ=⌈d/qk−1⌉⋅[k1]q≥n\Lambda=\left\lceil d/q^{k-1}\right\rceil\cdot\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k}{1}_{q}\geq n always works considering a tt-fold simplex code with t=⌈d/qk−1⌉t=\left\lceil d/q^{k-1}\right\rceil. ∎

We remark that we may also start with a rather small value for Λ\Lambda. If we find a feasible solution with target value nn, then we can deduce nq​(k,d,r)≤nn_{q}(k,d,r)\leq n. Using this nn we can utilize Inequality (4) to deduce an upper bound for Λ\Lambda.

Using indicator variables uP∈{0,1}u_{P}\in\{0,1\} for ℳ⁡(P)≥1\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 1 and zL∈{0,1}z_{L}\in\{0,1\} for lines LL containing at least three points with positive multiplicity we can adjust the previous ILP to model multisets of points with locality 22.

Let qq, kk, and dd be arbitrary but fixed parameters. Then, nq​(k,d,2)n_{q}(k,d,2) is given as the optimum target value of the following ILP:

where eie_{i} denotes the iith unit vector, 𝒫\mathcal{P} denotes the set of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q), ℒ\mathcal{L} denotes the set of lines in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q), ℋ\mathcal{H} denotes the set of hyperplanes in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q), and Λ\Lambda is a sufficiently large constant.

Lemma 13.

For each n≥nq​(k,d,r)n\geq n_{q}(k,d,r) there exists an [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-code with locality rr.

Proof.

Assume nq​(k,d,r)<∞n_{q}(k,d,r)<\infty. Let C′C^{\prime} be an [n′,k,d]q[n^{\prime},k,d]_{q}-code with n′=nq​(k,d,r)n^{\prime}=n_{q}(k,d,r) and locality rr. Consider the corresponding multiset of points ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime} in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) and let PP by an arbitrary point with positive multiplicity. Define the multiset of points ℳ\mathcal{M} in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) by setting ℳ​(Q)=ℳ′​(Q)\mathcal{M}(Q)=\mathcal{M}^{\prime}(Q) for all points Q≠PQ\neq P and ℳ⁡(P)=ℳ′​(P)+n−n′≥ℳ′​(P)\mathcal{M}(P)=\mathcal{M}^{\prime}(P)+n-n^{\prime}\geq\mathcal{M}^{\prime}(P). by construction we have |ℳ|=n|\mathcal{M}|=n and ℳ\mathcal{M} has locality rr. The linear code CC corresponding to ℳ\mathcal{M} also has minimum Hamming distance at least dd. ∎

The previous results are in principle sufficient to determine nq​(k,d,r)n_{q}(k,d,r) for small parameters qq, kk, and rr, so that we may just give tables of the obtained computational results. However, we prefer to give general constructions and non-existence results in the next section first.

4 Constructions and non-existence results

In this section we want to study some general constructions to upper bound nq​(k,d,r)n_{q}(k,d,r). To this end we denote the iith unit vector by eie_{i}, whenever the dimension of the ambient space is clear from the context, and for each subspace SS its characteristic function is denoted by χS\chi_{S}, i.e., χS​(P)=1\chi_{S}(P)=1 if P≤SP\leq S and χS​(P)=0\chi_{S}(P)=0 otherwise. In a few cases we can also give theoretical non-existence proofs for certain parameters to obtain lower bounds for nq​(k,d,r)n_{q}(k,d,r). First, let us define nq′​(k,r)n^{\prime}_{q}(k,r) as the minimum length nn of an [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-code with locality rr. Clearly, we have nq​(k,d,r)≥nq​(k,r)n_{q}(k,d,r)\geq n_{q}(k,r). As observed earlier, the maximum possible locality is given by r=kr=k and we have nq​(k,d,1)≥nq​(k,d,2)≥⋯≥nq​(k,d,k)n_{q}(k,d,1)\geq n_{q}(k,d,2)\geq\dots\geq n_{q}(k,d,k).

Proposition 14.

For each integer k≥1k\geq 1 we have nq′​(k,1)=2​kn^{\prime}_{q}(k,1)=2k and nq′​(k,2)=⌈3​k2⌉n^{\prime}_{q}(k,2)=\left\lceil\tfrac{3k}{2}\right\rceil.

Proof.

Let ℳ\mathcal{M} be a spanning multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) with locality 11. Due to Lemma 6 every point PP with positive multiplicity ℳ⁡(P)≥1\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 1 satisfies ℳ⁡(P)≥2\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 2. Since ℳ\mathcal{M} is spanning, it contains at least kk points with positive multiplicity, so that |ℳ|≥2​k|\mathcal{M}|\geq 2k. An attaining example is e.g. given by ℳ=∑i=1k2⋅χ⟨ei⟩\mathcal{M}=\sum_{i=1}^{k}2\cdot\chi_{\langle e_{i}\rangle}.

For the other case let ℳ\mathcal{M} be a spanning multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) with locality 22. Due to Lemma 7 every point PP with positive multiplicity ℳ⁡(P)≥1\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 1 either has multiplicity at least 22 or is contained in a line LL that contains at least three points of positive multiplicity. So, let {L1,…,Lm}\left\{L_{1},\dots,L_{m}\right\} be the set of those lines. For each index 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m let SiS_{i} be the subspace spanned by the points of the lines L1,…,LiL_{1},\dots,L_{i}. To also capture the case m=0m=0 let us denote the empty space by S0S_{0}. With this we have dim(S0)=0\dim(S_{0})=0, ℳ⁡(S0)=0\mathcal{M}(S_{0})=0, dim(S1)=2\dim(S_{1})=2, and ℳ⁡(S1)≥3\mathcal{M}(S_{1})\geq 3. For i≥2i\geq 2 we show ℳ⁡(Si)≤⌈3​dim(Si)/2⌉\mathcal{M}(S_{i})\leq\left\lceil 3\dim(S_{i})/2\right\rceil and dim(Si−1)≤dim(Si)≤dim(Si−1)+2\dim(S_{i-1})\leq\dim(S_{i})\leq\dim(S_{i-1})+2 by induction. So, if LiL_{i} is completely contained in Si−1S_{i-1}, then we have dim(Si)=dim(Si−1)\dim(S_{i})=\dim(S_{i-1}) and ℳ⁡(Si)=ℳ⁡(Si−1)\mathcal{M}(S_{i})=\mathcal{M}(S_{i-1}). If the intersection of Si−1S_{i-1} and LiL_{i} is non-empty but LiL_{i} is not completely contained in Si−1S_{i-1}, then Q:=Si−1∩LiQ:=S_{i-1}\cap L_{i} is a point. So, we have dim(Si)=dim(Si−1)+1\dim(S_{i})=\dim(S_{i-1})+1 and ℳ⁡(Si)≥ℳ⁡(Si−1)+2\mathcal{M}(S_{i})\geq\mathcal{M}(S_{i-1})+2. If the intersection of LiL_{i} and Si−1S_{i-1} is empty, then we have dim(Si)=dim(Si−1)+2\dim(S_{i})=\dim(S_{i-1})+2 and ℳ⁡(Si)≥ℳ⁡(Si−1)+3\mathcal{M}(S_{i})\geq\mathcal{M}(S_{i-1})+3. Now let us consider the set of points PP with positive multiplicity that are not contained in SmS_{m}. By construction, none of these points is contained in a line LL that contains at least three points with positive multiplicity. So, we have ℳ⁡(P)≥2\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 2 for each such point. Since ℳ\mathcal{M} is spanning we have at least k−dim(Sm)k-\dim(S_{m}) of those points and conclude

|ℳ|≥⌈3​dim(Sm)2⌉+2​(k−dim(Sm))≥⌈3​k2⌉.|\mathcal{M}|\geq\left\lceil\tfrac{3\dim(S_{m})}{2}\right\rceil+2\left(k-\dim(S_{m})\right)\geq\left\lceil\tfrac{3k}{2}\right\rceil.

For even kk an attaining example is given by the set of points

{⟨e2​i−1⟩,⟨e2​i⟩,⟨e2​i−1+e2​i⟩: 1≤i≤k/2}\left\{\langle e_{2i-1}\rangle,\langle e_{2i}\rangle,\langle e_{2i-1}+e_{2i}\rangle:\,1\leq i\leq k/2\right\}

and for odd kk and example is given the sum of 2⋅χ⟨ek⟩2\cdot\chi_{\langle e_{k}\rangle} and the characteristic function of the set of points

{⟨e2​i−1⟩,⟨e2​i⟩,⟨e2​i−1+e2​i⟩: 1≤i≤(k−1)/2}.\left\{\langle e_{2i-1}\rangle,\langle e_{2i}\rangle,\langle e_{2i-1}+e_{2i}\rangle:\,1\leq i\leq(k-1)/2\right\}.

∎

Corollary 15.

For each integer k≥1k\geq 1 we have nq​(k,1,2)=nq​(k,2,2)=⌈3​k2⌉n_{q}(k,1,2)=n_{q}(k,2,2)=\left\lceil\tfrac{3k}{2}\right\rceil.

Proof.

Due to Proposition 14 it suffices to state attaining examples and indeed we will just verify that the examples from the proof of Proposition 14 have minimum Hamming distance d=2d=2.

If kk is even let ℳ=∑i=1kχ⟨ei⟩+∑i=1k/2χ⟨e2​i−1+e2​i⟩\mathcal{M}=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\chi_{\langle e_{i}\rangle}\,+\,\sum_{i=1}^{k/2}\chi_{\langle e_{2i-1}+e_{2i}\rangle}, so that |ℳ|=3​k2|\mathcal{M}|=\tfrac{3k}{2}, ℳ\mathcal{M} is spanning, and has locality r=2r=2. For each 1≤i≤k/21\leq i\leq k/2 let LiL_{i} the the line spanned by the points ⟨e2​i−1⟩\langle e_{2i-1}\rangle, ⟨e2​i⟩\langle e_{2i}\rangle , and ⟨e2​i−1+e2​i⟩\langle e_{2i-1}+e_{2i}\rangle. For each hyperplane HH at most k/2−1k/2-1 lines LiL_{i} can be fully contained in HH and the others intersect in at most a point, so that ℳ⁡(H)≤3​k2−2\mathcal{M}(H)\leq\tfrac{3k}{2}-2. Thus, the linear code CC corresponding to ℳ\mathcal{M} has minimum Hamming distance d=2d=2.

If kk is odd let ℳ=∑i=1k−1χ⟨ei⟩+∑i=1(k−1)/2χ⟨e2​i−1+e2​i⟩+ 2⋅χ⟨ek⟩\mathcal{M}=\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}\chi_{\langle e_{i}\rangle}\,+\,\sum_{i=1}^{(k-1)/2}\chi_{\langle e_{2i-1}+e_{2i}\rangle}\,+\,2\cdot\chi_{\langle e_{k}\rangle}, so that |ℳ|=⌈3​k2⌉=3​k+12|\mathcal{M}|=\left\lceil\tfrac{3k}{2}\right\rceil=\tfrac{3k+1}{2}, ℳ\mathcal{M} is spanning, and has locality r=2r=2. For each 1≤i≤(k−1)/21\leq i\leq(k-1)/2 let LiL_{i} the the line spanned by the points ⟨e2​i−1⟩\langle e_{2i-1}\rangle, ⟨e2​i⟩\langle e_{2i}\rangle , and ⟨e2​i−1+e2​i⟩\langle e_{2i-1}+e_{2i}\rangle. By PP be denote the point ⟨ek⟩\langle e_{k}\rangle. For each hyperplane HH that contains PP at most (k−1)/2−1(k-1)/2-1 lines LiL_{i} can be fully contained in HH and the others intersect in at most a point, so that ℳ⁡(H)≤3​k+12−2\mathcal{M}(H)\leq\tfrac{3k+1}{2}-2. For each hyperplane HH that does not contain PP we also have ℳ⁡(H)≤3​k+12−2\mathcal{M}(H)\leq\tfrac{3k+1}{2}-2, so that the linear code CC corresponding to ℳ\mathcal{M} has minimum Hamming distance d=2d=2. ∎

Proposition 16.

For each integer k≥2k\geq 2 we have nq′​(k,k)=k+1n^{\prime}_{q}(k,k)=k+1.

Proof.

Let ℳ\mathcal{M} be a spanning multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) with locality kk. Since ℳ\mathcal{M} is spanning we have |ℳ|≥k|\mathcal{M}|\geq k. Up to symmetry the unique spanning multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) of cardinality kk is given by the set of points {⟨ei⟩: 1≤i≤k}\left\{\langle e_{i}\rangle\,:\,1\leq i\leq k\right\} which does have a finite locality. Thus, we have nq′​(k,k)≥k+1n^{\prime}_{q}(k,k)\geq k+1. An attaining example is given by the set of points

{⟨ei⟩: 1≤i≤k}∪{⟨∑i=1kei⟩}.\left\{\left\langle e_{i}\right\rangle\,:\,1\leq i\leq k\right\}\cup\left\{\left\langle\sum_{i=1}^{k}e_{i}\right\rangle\right\}.

Here we can easily check that each subset of kk points spans the entire ambient space. ∎

We remark that the point set of our construction is called projective base or frame in the literature. Due to Proposition 14 we also have nq′​(k,k)=k+1n^{\prime}_{q}(k,k)=k+1 for k=1k=1 and we may also consider the double-point 2⋅χ⟨e1⟩2\cdot\chi_{\langle e_{1}\rangle} as a degenerated cases of a projective base.

For small dimensions k≤2k\leq 2 the determination of nq​(k,d,r)n_{q}(k,d,r) can be resolved completely analytically:

Proposition 17.

We have nq​(1,d,r)=max⁡{2,d}n_{q}(1,d,r)=\max\{2,d\}, nq​(2,d,1)=2​⌈d2⌉+2n_{q}(2,d,1)=2\left\lceil\tfrac{d}{2}\right\rceil+2 if d<2​qd<2q, nq​(2,d,1)=d+⌈dq⌉n_{q}(2,d,1)=d+\left\lceil\frac{d}{q}\right\rceil if d≥2​qd\geq 2q, and nq​(2,d,r)=d+⌈dq⌉n_{q}(2,d,r)=d+\left\lceil\frac{d}{q}\right\rceil for r≥2r\geq 2.

Proof.

In PG⁡(1−1,q)\PG(1-1,q) the unique multiset of points with cardinality nn is given by ℳ=n⋅χ⟨e1⟩\mathcal{M}=n\cdot\chi_{\langle e_{1}\rangle} which does not have a finite locality if n=1n=1 and has locality 11 if n≥2n\geq 2. Since there are no hyperplanes in PG⁡(1−1,q)\PG(1-1,q) we need to observe that the non-zero weights of the codewords of the corresponding linear code CC all are equal to nn. Thus, we conclude nq​(1,d,r)=max⁡{2,d}n_{q}(1,d,r)=\max\{2,d\}.

Let ℳ\mathcal{M} be a spanning multiset of points of cardinality nn in PG⁡(2−1,q)\PG(2-1,q) and CC its corresponding linear code [n,k]q[n,k]_{q}-code. The minimum Hamming distance of CC is at least dd iff we have ℳ⁡(P)≤n−d\mathcal{M}(P)\leq n-d for every point PP. Let us uniquely write d=a​q+bd=aq+b with a∈ℕa\in\mathbb{N} and b∈{0,1,…,q−1}b\in\{0,1,\dots,q-1\}. With this we have

n≥nq​(k,d,r)≥nq​(k,d)≥gq​(k,d)=∑i=0k−1⌈dqi⌉=d+⌈dq⌉=a⁡(q+1)+b+⌈bq⌉.n\geq n_{q}(k,d,r)\geq n_{q}(k,d)\geq g_{q}(k,d)=\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left\lceil\frac{d}{q^{i}}\right\rceil=d+\left\lceil\frac{d}{q}\right\rceil=a(q+1)+b+\left\lceil\tfrac{b}{q}\right\rceil. (7)

Let LL denote the ambient space, which is a line in our situation. If b=0b=0 and a≥1a\geq 1, then a⋅χLa\cdot\chi_{L} attains this bound and has locality 22 (or 11 if a≥2a\geq 2). If b≥1b\geq 1 and a≥0a\geq 0, then the multiset of points given by the sum of a⋅χLa\cdot\chi_{L} and the characteristic function of arbitrary b+1≤qb+1\leq q different points on LL attains this bound and has locality 22 if a≥1a\geq 1 or b≥2b\geq 2; we even have locality 11 if a≥2a\geq 2. So, for locality r=2r=2 it remains to consider the case d=1d=1 where we can consider the multiset of points 2⋅χP2\cdot\chi_{P} for an arbitrary point PP. Thus, for r≥2r\geq 2 we have nq​(2,d,r)=d+⌈dq⌉n_{q}(2,d,r)=d+\left\lceil\frac{d}{q}\right\rceil and nq​(2,d,1)=d+⌈dq⌉n_{q}(2,d,1)=d+\left\lceil\frac{d}{q}\right\rceil if d≥2​qd\geq 2q.

For locality r=1r=1, dimension k=2k=2, and 1≤d<2​q1\leq d<2q each point PP in a multiset ℳ\mathcal{M} with these parameters satisfying ℳ⁡(P)≥1\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 1 indeed has to satisfy ℳ⁡(P)≥2\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 2. If we have l≤2l\leq 2 points with positive multiplicity, then we have n≥2​l+ℳ⁡(P)−2≥2​ln\geq 2l+\mathcal{M}(P)-2\geq 2l and d≤n−ℳ⁡(P)≤2​l−2d\leq n-\mathcal{M}(P)\leq 2l-2 for every point PP with positive multiplicity. Thus, for even 2≤d<2​q2\leq d<2q we have nq​(2,d,1)=d+2n_{q}(2,d,1)=d+2 and for odd 1≤d<2​q1\leq d<2q we have nq​(2,d,1)=d+3n_{q}(2,d,1)=d+3. ∎

For k≥3k\geq 3 we remark that even the determination of nq​(k,d)n_{q}(k,d) is a long-standing open problem for q>9q>9, so that we do not expect a closed-form solution for nq​(k,d,r)n_{q}(k,d,r) when k≥3k\geq 3.

A well-known construction for distance-optimal linear codes is due to Solomon and Stiffler [SS65].

Lemma 18.

Let k≥2k\geq 2,

n=σ​[k]q−∑i=0k−2εi​[i+11]q,n=\sigma[k]_{q}-\sum_{i=0}^{k-2}\varepsilon_{i}\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{i+1}{1}_{q},

and

n−d=σ​[k−1]q−∑i=1k−2εi​[i1]q,n-d=\sigma[k-1]_{q}-\sum_{i=1}^{k-2}\varepsilon_{i}\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{i}{1}_{q},

where σ∈ℕ\sigma\in\mathbb{N} and εi∈ℕ\varepsilon_{i}\in\mathbb{N} for all 0≤i≤k−20\leq i\leq k-2. If there exist subspaces S1,…,SlS_{1},\dots,S_{l} in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q) such that

#⁡{1≤j≤l:dim(Sj)=i}=εi+1\#\left\{1\leq j\leq l\,:\,\dim\!\left(S_{j}\right)=i\right\}=\varepsilon_{i+1} (8)

for 1≤i≤k−11\leq i\leq k-1 and

#⁡{1≤j≤l:P∈Sj}≤σ\#\left\{1\leq j\leq l\,:\,P\in S_{j}\right\}\leq\sigma (9)

for each point PP in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q), then an [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-code exists.

In terms of a multiset of points the underlying construction is given by ℳ=σ⋅χV−∑j=1lχSj\mathcal{M}=\sigma\cdot\chi_{V}-\sum\limits_{j=1}^{l}\chi_{S_{j}}, where VV denotes the ambient space PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q). In the literature mostly the case n=gk​(k,d)n=g_{k}(k,d) is considered, while the construction works of course in general. There are also many criteria available in the literature when those subspaces SjS_{j} exist given the other numerical parameters. Here we will just speak of a Solomon-Stifler construction of type [σ;εk−2,…,ε1,ε0]\left[\sigma;\varepsilon_{k-2},\dots,\varepsilon_{1},\varepsilon_{0}\right] and will mostly leave the existence proof for subspaces satisfying the conditions of Lemma 18 to the reader.

Example 19.

Let ℳ\mathcal{M} be the multiset of points in PG⁡(k−1,q)\PG(k-1,q), where k≥2k\geq 2, obtained from the Solomon-Stifler construction of type [1;1,0,…,0][1;1,0,\dots,0] and CC its corresponding [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-code. Then, we have n=[k1]q−[k−11]q=qk−1n=\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k}{1}_{q}-\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k-1}{1}_{q}=q^{k-1}, d=(q−1)​qk−2d=(q-1)q^{k-2}, and n=gq​(k,d)n=g_{q}(k,d). Note that the maximum point multiplicity of ℳ\mathcal{M} is 11 and that very line LL that contains two points of positive multiplicity has multiplicity ℳ⁡(L)=q\mathcal{M}(L)=q since LL intersects the subspace SiS_{i} in exactly a point. Thus, we have nq​(k,(q−1)​qk−2,2)=qk−1n_{q}(k,(q-1)q^{k-2},2)=q^{k-1} for all q≥3q\geq 3.

The just considered set of points is also known under the term affine subspace. For the binary case q=2q=2, where our construction does not give a multiset of points with locality 22, we can use the well-known result that each code with the above parameters can be obtained from the Solomon-Stifler construction of type [1;1,0,…,0][1;1,0,\dots,0], see e.g. [KY21, Lemma 12], to conclude:

Lemma 20.

For each k≥2k\geq 2 we have n2​(k,2k−2,2)≥2k−1+1n_{2}(k,2^{k-2},2)\geq 2^{k-1}+1.

Lemma 21.

Let C′C^{\prime} be a projective [n′,k′,d′]2[n^{\prime},k^{\prime},d^{\prime}]_{2}-code with k′≥2k^{\prime}\geq 2. Then, we have n2​(k′+1,min⁡{2​d′,n′+1},2)≤2​n′+1n_{2}(k^{\prime}+1,\min\!\left\{2d^{\prime},n^{\prime}+1\right\},2)\leq 2n^{\prime}+1.

Proof.

Let ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime} be a spanning multiset of points in PG⁡(k′−1,2)\PG(k^{\prime}-1,2) corresponding to C′C^{\prime}, so that ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime} has maximum point multiplicity 11. For each hyperplane H′H^{\prime} of PG⁡(k′−1,2)\PG(k^{\prime}-1,2) we have ℳ′​(H′)≤n′−d′\mathcal{M}^{\prime}(H^{\prime})\leq n^{\prime}-d^{\prime}. Let SS be a k′k^{\prime}-dimensional subspace in PG⁡(k−1,2)\PG(k-1,2), where k=k′+1k=k^{\prime}+1, and 𝒫\mathcal{P} be the set of points in PG⁡(k−1,2)\PG(k-1,2) that arise from an embedding of ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime} in SS. Choose an arbitrary point PP outside of SS and let ℒ\mathcal{L} be the set of lines spanned by PP and each element of 𝒫\mathcal{P}, so that |ℒ|=n′|\mathcal{L}|=n^{\prime}. With this, we define the multiset of points ℳ\mathcal{M} in PG⁡(k,2)\PG(k,2) as the characteristic function of the points contained in at least one line in ℒ\mathcal{L}, so that |ℳ|=2​n′+1|\mathcal{M}|=2n^{\prime}+1. For each hyperplane HH of PG⁡(k−1,2)\PG(k-1,2) that contains PP we have ℳ⁡(H)≤1+2​(n′−d′)\mathcal{M}(H)\leq 1+2(n^{\prime}-d^{\prime}) since at most n′−d′n^{\prime}-d^{\prime} lines of ℒ\mathcal{L} can be fully contained in HH. (The other lines intersect the hyperplane HH just in point PP.) For every other hyperplane HH in PG⁡(k−1,2)\PG(k-1,2), i.e. PP is not contained in HH, we have ℳ⁡(H)=n′\mathcal{M}(H)=n^{\prime} since any line in ℒ\mathcal{L} intersects HH in precisely a point. Thus, we have ℳ⁡(H)≤max⁡{1+2​(n′−d′),n′}\mathcal{M}(H)\leq\max\!\left\{1+2(n^{\prime}-d^{\prime}),n^{\prime}\right\}. So, for the linear code CC corresponding to ℳ\mathcal{M} is an [n,k,d]2[n,k,d]_{2}-code with n=2​n′+1n=2n^{\prime}+1, k=k′+1k=k^{\prime}+1 and d=min⁡{2​d′,n′+1}d=\min\!\left\{2d^{\prime},n^{\prime}+1\right\}. By construction, every point in PG⁡(k−1,2)\PG(k-1,2) with positive multiplicity w.r.t. ℳ\mathcal{M} lies on a line consisting of three points with positive multiplicity each. Thus, ℳ\mathcal{M} as well as CC have locality 22 and we can deduce the stated upper bound. ∎

Proposition 22.

Since ℳ\mathcal{M} arises from σ⋅χV\sigma\cdot\chi_{V} by decreasing point multiplicities by ∑i=0k−1εi⋅[i+11]q<σ⋅[k−11]q\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\varepsilon_{i}\cdot\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{i+1}{1}_{q}<\sigma\cdot\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{k-1}{1}_{q} and removing a point from the support costs multiplicity σ\sigma, at least one full line through PP remains if ℳ⁡(P)≥1\mathcal{M}(P)\geq 1. ∎

Applying the MacWilliams transform we then compute also the dual weight distribution of C′C^{\prime}. To this end let us slightly generalize Lemma 8 and the proof idea for n2​(5,7,2)>15n_{2}(5,7,2)>15.

Lemma 31.

Let CC be an [n,k,d]2[n,k,d]_{2}-code with odd minimum distance dd and C′C^{\prime} be the [n+1,k,d+1]2[n+1,k,d+1]_{2}-code obtained from CC by adding a parity check bit. Let ℳ\mathcal{M} and ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime} be the multisets of points corresponding to CC and C′C^{\prime}, respectively. Note that ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime} arises from ℳ\mathcal{M} by increasing the point multiplicity of a certain point PP by 11. Using the fact that the dual minimum distance of C′C^{\prime} is 33 we conclude that both ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime} and ℳ\mathcal{M} have a maximum point multiplicity of 11. Since C′C^{\prime} contains less than n/3n/3 dual codewords of weight 33, at most n−1n-1 points with positive multiplicity in ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime} can be contained in a line that is fully contained in the support of ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime}. Thus, there exists a point Q≠PQ\neq P with ℳ⁡(Q)=1\mathcal{M}(Q)=1 that is not contained in line LL that is fully contained in the support of ℳ\mathcal{M}. Using Lemma 7 we conclude that the locality of ℳ\mathcal{M} and CC is at least 33. ∎

Lemma 32.

For each t∈ℕ≥2t\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2} we have nq​(2​t,4,2)≤3​t+3n_{q}(2t,4,2)\leq 3t+3 and n2​(2​t+1,4,2)≤3​t+5n_{2}(2t+1,4,2)\leq 3t+5.

Proof.

Consider the tt triples of points Li={e2​i−1,e2​i,e2​i−1+e2​i}L_{i}=\left\{e_{2i-1},e_{2i},e_{2i-1}+e_{2i}\right\} for 1≤i≤t1\leq i\leq t, the triple of points L′={∑i=1te2​i−1,∑i=1te2​i,∑i=12​tei}L^{\prime}=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{t}e_{2i-1},\sum_{i=1}^{t}e_{2i},\sum_{i=1}^{2t}e_{i}\right\}, and the triple of points L′′={∑i=1t+1e2​i−1,∑i=1te2​i,∑i=12​t+1ei}L^{\prime\prime}=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{t+1}e_{2i-1},\sum_{i=1}^{t}e_{2i},\sum_{i=1}^{2t+1}e_{i}\right\}. (Over 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2} these triples are full lines.) With this let ℳ=χL′+∑i=1tχLi\mathcal{M}=\chi_{L^{\prime}}+\sum_{i=1}^{t}\chi_{L_{i}} and ℳ′=2⋅χP+χL′′+∑i=1tχLi\mathcal{M}^{\prime}=2\cdot\chi_{P}+\chi_{L^{\prime\prime}}+\sum_{i=1}^{t}\chi_{L_{i}}, where P=⟨e2​t+1⟩P=\langle e_{2t+1}\rangle. Note that ℳ\mathcal{M} spans PG⁡(2​t−1,q)\PG(2t-1,q), ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime} spans PG⁡(2​t,q)\PG(2t,q), |ℳ|=3​t+3|\mathcal{M}|=3t+3, |ℳ′|=3​t+5|\mathcal{M}^{\prime}|=3t+5, and both multisets of points have locality r=2r=2. So, it remains to upper bound the multiplicities of the hyperplanes of the respective ambient spaces. By construction, the multiplicities of H∩L′H\cap L^{\prime}, H∩L′′H\cap L^{\prime\prime}, and H∩LiH\cap L_{i}, where 1≤i≤t1\leq i\leq t, are not equal to 22 for each hyperplane HH.

Let us first consider ℳ\mathcal{M} in PG⁡(2​t−1,q)\PG(2t-1,q). Note that a hyperplane HH cannot fully contain all LiL_{i} for 1≤i≤t1\leq i\leq t. Due to symmetry we assume that L1L_{1} is not fully contained in HH. If also another triple LiL_{i} with 2≤i≤t2\leq i\leq t is not fully contained in HH, then we have ℳ⁡(H)≤3​t+3−2⋅2\mathcal{M}(H)\leq 3t+3-2\cdot 2. So, let us assume that HH fully contains all triples LiL_{i} for 2≤i≤t2\leq i\leq t. If |H∩L1|=1\left|H\cap L_{1}\right|=1, then due to symmetry we assume ⟨e1⟩≤H\left\langle e_{1}\right\rangle\leq H, so that HH is uniquely determined and we have ℳ⁡(H)≤3​t+3−2⋅2\mathcal{M}(H)\leq 3t+3-2\cdot 2 since L′L^{\prime} is not fully contained in HH. If |H∩L1|=0\left|H\cap L_{1}\right|=0 then L′L^{\prime} cannot be fully contained in HH, so that ℳ⁡(H)≤3​t+3−5\mathcal{M}(H)\leq 3t+3-5.

Next consider ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime} in PG⁡(2​t,q)\PG(2t,q). There is a unique hyperplane HH that fully contains LiL_{i} for 1≤i≤t1\leq i\leq t. Here we have ℳ′​(H)≤3​t+5−4\mathcal{M}^{\prime}(H)\leq 3t+5-4 since HH does not contain PP and also does not fully contain L′′L^{\prime\prime}. In the remaining cases we assume due to symmetry that HH does not fully contain L1L_{1}. If also another triple LiL_{i} with 2≤i≤t2\leq i\leq t is not fully contained in HH, then we have ℳ⁡(H)≤3​t+5−2⋅2\mathcal{M}(H)\leq 3t+5-2\cdot 2. Similarly, if HH does not fully contain L′′L^{\prime\prime}, then we have ℳ⁡(H)≤3​t+5−2⋅2\mathcal{M}(H)\leq 3t+5-2\cdot 2. So, let us assume that HH fully contains all triples LiL_{i} for 2≤i≤t2\leq i\leq t and also fully contains L′′L^{\prime\prime}. However, then there is a unique possibility for HH and we can easily check that PP is not contained in HH and we also have ℳ⁡(H)≤3​t+5−2⋅2\mathcal{M}(H)\leq 3t+5-2\cdot 2. ∎

Note that the upper bounds in Lemma 32 are valid for t<2t<2 also while there are better constructions for dimension k=1k=1 and dimension k=3k=3, when q=2q=2. In Table 2 we will see that there are 4141 [12,6,4]2[12,6,4]_{2}-codes while only the example from Lemma 32 has locality r=2r=2.

We remark that our stated [18,6,8]2[18,6,8]_{2}-code is a projective two-weight code. It belongs to the family of BY codes [BE97]. A [26,6,12]2[26,6,12]_{2}-code with locality r=2r=2 can be obtained by shortening the unique [27,7,12]2[27,7,12]_{2}-code.22 2 Uniqueness was e.g. computationally verified in [BJ01]. For a purely theoretic argument see “The uniqueness of the binary linear [27,7,12][27,7,12] code” by A. E. Brouwer from April 1992, available at https://www.win.tue.nl/∼\simaeb/preprints.html. There is a unique [38,6,18]2[38,6,18]_{2}-code, see e.g. [BJ01], shortening gives [37,6,17]2[37,6,17]_{2}-codes with locality r=2r=2. Note that both codes attain the Griesmer bound, see e.g. [Hel83] for constructions of binary codes attaining the Griesmer bound when d>2k−1d>2^{k-1}. We remark that there are 77 non-isomorphic [43,7,20]2[43,7,20]_{2} codes, see e.g. [BJ01], and all their shortenings yield [42,6,20]2[42,6,20]_{2}-codes with locality r=2r=2.

Lemma 35.

We have nq​(k,2​d′,1)≤2⋅nq​(k,d′)n_{q}(k,2d^{\prime},1)\leq 2\cdot n_{q}(k,d^{\prime}), nq​(k,d′+2⋅qk−1,1)≤2⋅(qk−1)/(q−1)+nq​(k,d′)n_{q}(k,d^{\prime}+2\cdot q^{k-1},1)\leq 2\cdot\left(q^{k}-1\right)/(q-1)+n_{q}(k,d^{\prime}), and nq​(k,3​d′−1,1)≤3⋅nq​(k,d′)−1n_{q}(k,3d^{\prime}-1,1)\leq 3\cdot n_{q}(k,d^{\prime})-1.

Proof.

If ℳ\mathcal{M} is the multiset of points corresponding to an [n′,k,d′]q[n^{\prime},k,d^{\prime}]_{q}-code, then 2⋅ℳ2\cdot\mathcal{M} corresponds to an [2​n′,k,2​d′]q[2n^{\prime},k,2d^{\prime}]_{q}-code with locality 11 since each point has an even multiplicity. Denoting the ambient space by AA, we have that ℳ+2⋅χA\mathcal{M}+2\cdot\chi_{A} corresponds to an [2⋅(qk−1)/(q−1)+n′,k,2⋅qk−1+d′]q\left[2\cdot\left(q^{k}-1\right)/(q-1)+n^{\prime},k,2\cdot q^{k-1}+d^{\prime}\right]_{q}-code with locality r=1r=1 since each point has multiplicity at least 22. Observing that 3⋅ℳ3\cdot\mathcal{M} corresponds to an [3​n′,k,3​d′]q[3n^{\prime},k,3d^{\prime}]_{q}-code with locality 11 since each point has an multiplicity that is divisible, we can decrease the point multiplicity of one point with positive multiplicity by one to obtain an [3​n′−1,k,3​d′−1]q[3n^{\prime}-1,k,3d^{\prime}-1]_{q}-code. ∎

We remark that all [69,4,45]3[69,4,45]_{3}-codes that have locality r=1r=1, when considered as a multiset of points in PG⁡(3,3)\PG(3,3), have maximum point multiplicity of at least 44 (and not 33 as in all other stated examples for the other parameters).

5 Enumeration results

Instead of solving ILPs to determine locally recoverable codes with the minimum possible length nq​(k,d,r)n_{q}(k,d,r) one may also enumerate all [n,k,d]q[n,k,d]_{q}-codes with minimum possible length n=nq​(k,d)n=n_{q}(k,d) or slightly larger length and check whether those codes have relatively small locality constants rr. For those enumerations we have applied the software LinCode [BBK21]. We present our computational results in Tables 1, 2, and 3. Locality r=1r=1 did not occur in any of these cases.

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.
